correctness.rationale: The externally proved Kaneko--Stoll Theorem 2.2 has the exact strict product bound 2^{-13+4lm}, specializing to 2^{23} at l=m=3. All odd three-bit positive numbers below the bound are uniquely 1+2^i+2^j with 1<=i<j<=22 (231 possibilities). The supplied exact verifier enumerates all product-admissible unordered factor pairs (3672), finding exactly six; a separate product-enumeration and divisor test independently recovers all six. All six satisfy the digit-weight assertions. Exhaustiveness is finite mathematical computation using unbounded integers, not inference from partial sampling.

originality.rationale: Theorem 2.2 of Kaneko--Stoll proves an upper bound but gives no enumeration of the (3,3,3) fibre. The six-element solution set is an exact invariant not entailed as a stated result by that upper bound. The related public (3,2,3) classification changes a factor weight and cannot cover any (3,3,3) pair. The square instance (7,7) is already covered by known square-weight work; originality is claimed for the complete six-case classification, not for each constituent example. Searches of published records and searchable mathematical literature, plus accessible archived claims, revealed no equivalent exact list. Remaining risk: unindexed or implicit prior classification.

value.rationale: The object is the natural symmetric (3,3,3) fibre of the explicit multiplicative digit-sum Diophantine system of Kaneko--Stoll. The exact set of six unordered solutions and eleven ordered solutions is a complete arithmetic classification, strengthening effective finiteness to an explicit answer for the first symmetric nontrivial three-bit instance. The fact separates all five off-diagonal solutions from the previously studied diagonal square and is useful as a benchmark for sharper carry-based classification techniques. This is a modest exact finite theorem; no downstream general theorem or universal digit-weight statement is claimed.
